sections.heading: Custom Screen Rules (beta)
items: Rules now react like the Block YouTube Shorts and Block Instagram Reels switches: they only fire while their screen is actually showing. Hidden or off-screen elements are ignored, and a tab captured while it was highlighted only counts while it is highlighted.
Open the screen you want blocked and select its tab before you capture, so FocusFlow can tell the difference. The guide and the AI prompt both explain this.

New Test this rule button in the rule editor, just above Save. Switch to the app, open a screen, and it tells you whether the rule would block it and what each element found (found, not selected, hidden, or not on this screen). Nothing is blocked during a test, and you can test before saving.

Choose element has a Screen view (rebuilt from element positions and text, no screenshot is taken) and a Text list, side by side like Privacy and Terms. You can Export the scan and Capture again from there.
New Guide (Beta) - How to use page: steps for making a rule yourself, plus a copyable prompt for an AI assistant that turns an exported scan into rules you can import.
A new My rules screen holds your rules and their switches. Custom Screen Rules is now a simple home with My rules, Add rule from screen, Add rule manually, Import / export and the guide.
Custom rule screens now stay clear of the system navigation bar, with both 3-button and gesture navigation.

sections.heading: Phone usage analytics
items: Stats is back to its original layout with a compact Phone habits card and one button into Extra. Extra has Overview, Apps and Habits tabs and one period menu: Today, Yesterday, Week and All time.
Habit nudges can now also come from your phone habits (a surge, a time-of-day habit, late-night use). They are opt-in and limited to three, with the switch in Extra - Habits.
How usage data is calculated now lives on one page in Settings - About, instead of on each card.
Stats and Extra headers now follow your screen and text size like the other tabs, instead of a fixed height.
The How was today / yesterday prompt scrolls with the page and goes away once you answer it.
Achievements were removed from Overview and All-time stats.

sections.heading: Reporting a problem
items: Long logs now drop the oldest lines instead of the newest ones, and your own message is no longer scrubbed of e-mail addresses or links (secrets are still removed).
You can share the full log as a .txt file from the report screen.
Task-end alarm problems now record their cause in the log so they can be diagnosed.

sections.heading: Blocking
items: WhatsApp (and WhatsApp Business) is no longer a hard-protected app that silently ignored blocks. It now works like the SMS apps: the app picker warns first, and once you confirm, the block really applies.

sections.heading: Subtasks and rich imports
items: Subtasks let you tick off parts of a task, with steps, goals, images, and a rest timer. Import files can now include subtasks and images.
Image-rich .focusflow files can use ZIP bundles; files with subtasks or images declare version 2, while task-only files remain version 1.
Exercise goals support rep ranges through repsMax, such as 6–10 reps, and imported or attached images stay stored privately on your device.

sections.heading: Photo slots
items: Task files can now describe a picture with a short brief and an optional link instead of carrying image data. Items show Photo needed until you attach one.

You can download the pictures a file linked to (only after you confirm), add several pictures in order, copy picture prompts for an image tool, and reuse a picture you already have when an item has the same name.
Downloaded pictures are checked, resized and stored privately on your device. Links are never opened in a browser.

sections.heading: Rewritten in Kotlin
items: FocusFlow has been rewritten as a native Android app in Kotlin, with every screen built in Jetpack Compose.
Tasks, Focus sessions, app blocking, Defense, Stats and Settings now run in one native codebase instead of a React Native and Kotlin hybrid.
Your existing .focusflow backup files still import, so tasks and settings can be restored.

sections.heading: Home Launcher
items: Added Classic and Glassy launcher themes with wallpaper-aware styling, a focused home layout, and configurable app-drawer controls.
Updated the fixed FocusFlow launcher shortcut to use the official FocusFlow app icon in both themes and their configuration previews.

sections.heading: Focus Session Reliability
items: Fixed stale Focus Mode and timed standalone state lingering after a session expired or the device restarted, so old sessions no longer keep apps blocked.
Deferred enforcement actions now re-check the current session state before redirecting or dismissing screens, preventing delayed callbacks from acting on an ended focus session.
